### How it works

1. **Thesis first.** Each trade's reasoning, entry, stop and exit conditions are committed before the trade is posted.
2. **No edits.** A published file is never changed. Corrections are new, dated files.
3. **Nothing deleted.** Losing trades stay in the record.
4. **Independently timestamped.** Every push gets GitHub's own receipt and a proof anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain.

<sub>This is a model portfolio: the reference book for my trading. Live execution follows the same theses, though sizing and timing can differ, so results are not an account statement. Rules: [methodology](methodology/v1.md).</sub>

---

<details>
<summary><b>What this record proves, and what it doesn't</b></summary>

The commit history proves the order and content of every entry, and that nothing has been rewritten. GitHub's [push log](https://github.com/mcmrwallst/mcmr-track-record/activity?ref=main&sort=asc) shows when every push arrived, and anyone can open it. The files in [`/receipts`](receipts/) carry GitHub's own server-side record of when each commit arrived, independently confirmable via GH Archive, and OpenTimestamps proofs anchor the same to the Bitcoin blockchain. Trades are also posted live on [X (@mcmrwallst)](https://x.com/mcmrwallst), and every post ID carries X's own creation time: a second clock, outside GitHub.

Prices are the levels at the moment each decision was made, published with it and checked against that day's traded range. As a model portfolio, they record the decision rather than a broker fill. What the record offers is reasoning fixed in public before the outcome, to be judged on its merits rather than reconstructed afterwards.

Full detail, including every known departure from the rules: [VERIFICATION.md](VERIFICATION.md).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Ledger rules in full</b></summary>

1. **Commit first, post second.** The push happens before, or at the same time as, any public post about the trade. Where a lag exists between the stated entry time and the commit, the lag is stated in the file.
2. **Never edit a published trade file.** Not for typos, not for clarifications, not within the hour. Corrections and additions get a new dated UPDATE file that references the original. Past departures from this rule are listed in [VERIFICATION.md](VERIFICATION.md) rather than left to be found.
3. **Sign every commit.** Unsigned commits establish no authorship; the author field is free text that anyone can set.
4. **One file per trade event** in `/trades`, named `YYYY-MM-DD_TICKER_ACTION.md` (for example `2026-07-22_ES_OPEN.md`).
5. **Losers stay.** Nothing is deleted. A ledger you can prune is a highlight reel.
6. **Archives** (X data export, screenshots) go in `/archives`; committing them stamps the date of possession.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Repository structure</b></summary>

```
mcmr-track-record/
├── PERFORMANCE.md    # returns, drawdowns, trades (generated)

├── trades/           # one file per trade event
├── performance/      # registry, marks, prices, reports, charts

├── templates/
└── scripts/
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Verify it yourself</b></summary>

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mcmrwallst/mcmr-track-record
cd mcmr-track-record
git log --oneline --graph          # full sequence, nothing pruned
git log -p --follow -- trades/     # every edit ever made to any trade file

pip install opentimestamps-client
ots verify receipts/<commit-sha>.json.ots
```

How to confirm the push receipts against a third-party mirror that does not depend on this account existing is in [VERIFICATION.md](VERIFICATION.md).

</details>
